name: Assisted Pull-Up
equipmentItems: Assisted pull-up machine with kneeling pad
grip: Overhand pronated grip on overhead handles, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
description: Perform a vertical pull-up while kneeling on a counterbalanced weight pad, reducing effective bodyweight to build pulling strength and technique across a full range of motion.
setup: Select the counterbalance weight on the machine stack (higher weight provides more assistance; lower weight provides less).
Grasp the overhead handles with an overhand pronated grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Step onto the foot assist and place both knees securely onto the padded counterbalance lever.
Lower into a full dead hang with arms extended and core braced.
instructions: Pull your body upward by driving your elbows down and back toward your ribcage.
Continue pulling until your chin comfortably clears the height of the handles, keeping your chest lifted toward the bar.
Pause briefly at the top peak contraction, squeezing your lats.
Lower your body slowly under control, resisting the upward push of the knee pad until arms are fully extended at the bottom.
cues: Drive elbows down to your pockets.
Chest up, chin over the handles.
Lower with control to full arm extension.
commonMistakes: Kicking off the counterbalance pad to bounce out of the bottom.
Cutting the bottom range short without reaching full arm extension.
Shrugging shoulders into the neck at the top of the pull.

logging.example: Selected 30 kg assistance load on stack: record 30 kg counterbalance assistance (effective load = bodyweight - 30 kg).
logging.note: Higher stack load equals greater assistance; record the selected counterbalance pin load. Document athlete bodyweight for net workload.

variantNote: Counterbalanced vertical pull using a kneeling lever pad. Allows precise load progression toward unassisted bodyweight pull-ups.
